newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Dec 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Cathay Pacific has launched a localisation plan to strengthen its image as a local airline. It would increase Cantonese and Mandarin-speaking cabin crew staff by 300-500 every year.
--The government was considering the introduction of an open-examination system as soon as possible to give foreign barristers the chance to practise in Hong Kong.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Hong Kong's leader-in-waiting Tung Chee-hwa hinted he was confident Beijing trusted him and would not reject his list of post-handover administrators.

-- WEN WEI PO -- China had approved the fourth lot of 38 enterprises to be listed on overseas markets. A spokesman said the enterprises represented the overall development level and potential of the Chinese economy.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A hotel and tourism consultancy said the resurgence of hotel development in China after the relaxation of credit controls and improvements in the investment environment will put pressure on some cities in the next two years.
-- Insurance brokers were identifying ways to get around new anti-discrimination laws so they could continue to charge higher premiums to those they considered to be greater risks.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Director of Audit Dominic Chan expressed concern over his post-handover autonomy and said he was hoping for assurances from Chief Executive-designate Tung.

-- Companies planning to list on the Hong Kong stock exchange faced tough competition from China-related stocks making their debut as mainland companies became the hot picks of investors and analysts.
